clue.text: Like Canute, for instance? That's ———!

parts.note: like means in the manner of, as
Canute was an English and Danish king of the eleventh century

explanation.surface: A quizzer compares someone to old Canute, then fills in a familiar exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is the exclamation 'That's asking!', said of a question too hard or too cheeky to answer. Canute famously ordered the tide back, so 'like Canute' also hints at an unreasonable request.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom fills the blank: 'That's asking' is said of a demand that expects too much.

clue.text: Secure tie perhaps for a lonely man

parts.note: to anchor is to secure firmly

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word tie is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Fastening a tie may be just the thing for a solitary man.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorite is a religious recluse who lives alone, withdrawn from the world.

clue.text: Did plain needlework

parts.note: plain is the basic stitch worked with two needles and wool, so plain needlework is done with needles rather than thread

explanation.definitionFit: Plain is the basic stitch of work with wool on two needles, so doing it is working with yarn.

clue.text: Mixture of tar in 502 cc aqua fortis

indicators.note: a mixture blends the following letters into a new order

parts.note: 502 in Roman numerals is D (500) and II (2)
cc is the abbreviation for cubic centimetres, here simply its letters

explanation.surface: A chemist mixes tar into a measured amount of aqua fortis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixture of' rearranges TAR, IN, DII and CC.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua fortis, Latin for strong water, is the old name for this corrosive acid.

clue.text: Cloth has edges trimmed in readiness

indicators.note: has means holds within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: pared means trimmed at the edges, as with a knife
rep is a ribbed fabric, a crossword staple for cloth

explanation.surface: A piece of fabric has been neatly hemmed, ready for use.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in readiness is set up and good to go, made ready beforehand.

clue.text: Do, their accounts go with a bang?

definitions.text: Do, their accounts go with a bang?

parts.words: Do, their accounts go with a bang?
parts.note: journalists give accounts of events, and a report is also the loud bang of a gun

explanation.surface: A question whether some people's stories are explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: A report is both a journalist's account and the sound of a gunshot, so these people's accounts go bang.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists write accounts, and things that go bang make a report.

clue.text: Smoke and drink in quantity

definitions.meaning: a tobacco smoker's bowl and stem
a large cask of wine, holding about 105 gallons

explanation.definitionFit: A smoker's bowl and a big wine cask share the same name.

clue.text: Curling waves?

parts.note: cylinders used to curl hair, and also long breaking sea swells

explanation.definitionFit: Long curling swells of the sea and hair curlers both go by this name.

clue.text: Erotic game?

parts.note: erotic in its root sense of Eros, the love god who shoots arrows, so a game of throwing small arrows

explanation.definitionFit: The pub game of throwing small arrows at a board recalls Cupid's love arrows.

clue.text: Musically King Cole sounds a little flier

indicators.note: sounds says the next letters are spoken and heard, a sound-alike

parts.note: Nat King Cole was an American singer and pianist

explanation.surface: The singer Nat King Cole's music sounds like a small bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent G means the insect is said the same as the singer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a tiny flying insect.

clue.text: Bristol's bridge school

definitions.meaning: the ... Suspension Bridge spans the Avon Gorge at Bristol, an English city
... College is a well-known independent school in Bristol

explanation.definitionFit: The Bristol suburb gives its name both to Brunel's suspension bridge and to a famous public school.

clue.text: Disco music, universal god of the people

parts.note: disco is a style of pop music
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing
a lar is a Roman household god, one of the lares

explanation.surface: Dance-floor music has a mass appeal, as if a god of everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something popular belongs to or is liked by ordinary citizens generally.

clue.text: Are mechanics on strike in their shops

definitions.text: Are mechanics on strike in their shops

parts.note: workers on strike are out
fitters are mechanics who assemble and repair machinery

explanation.surface: A question whether striking mechanics stay at their workshops.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue asks who is found in shops selling clothes: clothiers sit in their shops, and the wordplay is striking mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing sellers keep shops, and the clue pictures them there as tradesmen whose name splits into strikers and mechanics.

clue.text: Letters for sweet manufacturers

definitions.meaning: the letter B written out twice in the plural, Bs
honey makers, the insects of the hive

explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the letter's name sounds and is spelt the same as the honey-making insects.

clue.text: Illnesses many apparent in humble dwellings

indicators.note: in means placed within, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: cots are small humble cottages
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many
plain means clear, apparent

explanation.surface: Sickness is evident in many poor homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints are ailments or disorders of the body.

clue.text: As Americans they're neither Asians nor necessarily communists

definitions.text: As Americans they're neither Asians nor necessarily communists

parts.words: As Americans they're neither Asians nor necessarily communists
parts.note: the native peoples of the Americas share a name with people of a South Asian country, and the dated term 'Red' for them is no mark of communism

explanation.surface: A remark sorting out which Americans are neither from Asia nor Reds.
explanation.walkthrough: Native Americans were long called 'Red' men in old Westerns, so 'communists' plays on that colour; the same name also covers people of India, hence 'Asians'.
explanation.definitionFit: The name given to native peoples of America also means people from India, an Asian nation.

clue.text: Prolonged and desperate appeal to include tune-up

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, putting a piece inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A long, frantic plea to tune up an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TUNE into ENUT, which goes inside SOS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sostenuto is a musical direction meaning sustained, notes held.

clue.text: Self-centred people show energy in new sites

indicators.note: in means placed inside the reworked word
new tells us the letters of sites are made anew in another order

parts.note: go means energy, as in get-up-and-go

explanation.surface: Egotists are bustling around fresh building sites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns SITES into EISTS, and 'in' puts GO inside it after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoists put themselves first, thinking chiefly of their own interest.

clue.text: Make good progress in the plant

explanation.definitionFit: The blue-flowered veronica shares its name with the phrase for going fast and well.

clue.text: Necessitates no right to the inner parts

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: entrails are the guts, the inner parts of a body

explanation.surface: Something requires that nobody has a claim to the innards.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve as an inevitable consequence, to make something necessary.

clue.text: Aimed to be educated

definitions.meaning: pointed a gun at a target

explanation.definitionFit: A gun pointed at a target, and a person taught a skill, are both described the same way.

clue.text: Above all, quietly resume order

indicators.note: order means put in a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Most importantly, restart proceedings calmly and in an orderly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest, standing over every other in rank.

clue.text: Raise to a position not without its obligations

definitions.text: Raise to a position not without its obligations

parts.words: Raise to a position not without its obligations
parts.note: the French saying noblesse oblige says rank brings duties, so to raise someone to the peerage is to give them obligations

explanation.surface: Promote someone to a post that carries duties.
explanation.walkthrough: Noblesse oblige: noble rank brings duties.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone a peer is to raise them in rank, which by tradition carries duties.

clue.text: Drink 'in the pasture

definitions.meaning: an alcoholic drink brewed from honey
a poetic word for a meadow

explanation.definitionFit: The honey wine and the old word for a grassy field share one spelling.

clue.text: Minimal causes of eye-trouble

parts.note: tiny specks of dust that get in the eye, as in the biblical speck in your brother's eye

explanation.definitionFit: Motes are tiny particles of dust, the kind that irritate an eye.

clue.text: Checked, tension in the plant

indicators.note: in means placed within, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: a reed is a tall waterside grass
strain means tension, stress

explanation.surface: Inspected the stress on a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory, but it is the grass REED, which holds STRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Checked here means held back or kept under control.

clue.text: Carry to terrible extremes

indicators.note: extremes means the first and last letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Bear something to awful lengths.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to lug or haul something along.

clue.text: This vegetable said to be a pulse

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a beat is a single pulse of the heart

explanation.surface: A vegetable said to be a legume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' tempts as a bean or lentil, but it is the heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The beet is a root vegetable, as in beetroot or sugar beet.

clue.text: Anne out for a trip in the back of a car

indicators.note: going for a trip suggests the letters are tripped up and jumbled

explanation.surface: Anne heads out on a journey in the back seat of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a trip' rearranges the letters of ANNE OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonneau is the rear passenger compartment of an open motor car.

clue.text: So one cricketer incompetent, it may be held?

definitions.text: So one cricketer incompetent, it may be held?

parts.words: So one cricketer incompetent, it may be held?
parts.note: a cricket side has eleven players; if one is unable, the remaining ten are able, and the phrase also means capable of being held

explanation.surface: One poor cricketer in the team, so perhaps a catch can still be held.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket team is eleven players: one being incompetent leaves ten capable, and run together that phrase means defensible.
explanation.definitionFit: A position that may be held is defensible, maintainable against attack.

clue.text: Southern issue which may induce revolution…

parts.note: an edition is one issue of a newspaper or magazine

explanation.surface: A Southern newspaper issue that might stir up rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is speech or action inciting rebellion against the state.

clue.text: In a bigwig too!

parts.note: a swell is a grand, important or fashionable person

explanation.surface: A grand personage in a big wig, as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means also, in addition.
